public_rationale: SoftBank retained its LTV policy and completed a further $30 billion OpenAI investment by October 1, 2026. This is material evidence of continuing funding capacity, but it does not establish sustained $40 billion annual funding. Conversely, a smaller contribution does not demonstrate inability. Neither early-resolution condition is met, and the speaker supplied no deadline.
limitations: The original round's headline amount includes potential syndication.
A financing policy is not a fixed dollar borrowing ceiling.
No finite period was specified for 'continue'.

statement.excerpt: This is especially true for Softbank. Based on its current promise to not borrow more than 25% of its holdings, it is near-impossible that SoftBank will be able to continue funding OpenAI at this rate ($40 billion a year), and $40 billion a year may not actually be enough.
statement.document_title: OpenAI Is A Systemic Risk To The Tech Industry

continue funding OpenAI at this rate ($40 billion a year)
$40 billion a year may not actually be enough
our_interpretation: The checkable forecast is that SoftBank cannot sustain approximately $40 billion of its own annual funding to OpenAI while retaining the stated financing policy.
'Continue' requires repeated annual funding after the 2025 round. A single funding announcement does not demonstrate sustained capacity.
Count SoftBank's own funded contribution, excluding amounts syndicated to other investors and counting completed funding separately from commitments.
The policy concerns adjusted net debt relative to holdings, rather than a simple ceiling on gross borrowing.
The suggestion that $40 billion 'may not' be enough supplies neither a firm outcome nor a period and is not separately scored.
criteria.support_condition: While retaining the policy, SoftBank demonstrably cannot meet recurring approximately $40 billion annual OpenAI funding requirements because of the financing constraint, rather than choosing a smaller investment.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Verified repeated annual contributions around $40 billion after the 2025 round, together with compliance with the stated policy and demonstrated continuing financing capacity, refute the claimed near-impossibility.
